title: Browser Privacy Hardening Checklist - Complete Security Guide
metaDescription: Complete browser privacy hardening checklist for Chrome, Firefox, Safari & Brave. Essential settings to protect your data and browsing privacy.
intro: Protect your online privacy with this comprehensive browser hardening checklist. Learn essential settings and configurations for Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Brave, and privacy-focused browsers like Incognito Browser to minimize tracking and secure your browsing data.

items.why: Third-party cookies allow advertisers and trackers to follow you across websites, building detailed profiles of your browsing habits.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Cookies > Block third-party cookies. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Enhanced Tracking Protection > Strict. Safari: Preferences > Privacy > Prevent cross-site tracking.

items.why: Sends a signal to websites requesting they don't track your browsing activity, though compliance is voluntary.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Send a 'Do Not Track' request. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Send websites a 'Do Not Track' signal. Safari: Preferences > Privacy > Website tracking > Ask websites not to track me.

items.why: Prevents websites from accessing your precise location data without explicit permission for each request.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Site Settings > Location > Don't allow sites to see your location. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Permissions > Location > Settings > Block new requests. Safari: Preferences > Websites > Location.

items.why: Regularly removes cookies, cache, and browsing history that can be used to track you or reconstruct your online activities.
items.howTo: Set browsers to clear data on exit or use private/incognito mode by default. Consider switching to Incognito Browser for automatic privacy protection without manual configuration.

items.why: JavaScript can be used for sophisticated tracking techniques including device fingerprinting that uniquely identify your browser.
items.howTo: Firefox: about:config > privacy.resistFingerprinting = true. Use browser extensions like uBlock Origin or NoScript. Brave blocks fingerprinting by default.

items.why: Encrypts DNS queries to prevent ISPs and network administrators from seeing which websites you visit.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Security > Use secure DNS. Firefox: Settings > General > Network Settings > Enable DNS over HTTPS. Use providers like Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Quad9.

items.task: Disable WebRTC to prevent IP leaks
items.why: WebRTC can reveal your real IP address even when using a VPN, compromising your privacy and location anonymity.
items.howTo: Chrome: Use extension to disable WebRTC. Firefox: about:config > media.peerconnection.enabled = false. Consider browsers like Incognito Browser that have WebRTC disabled by default.

items.why: Default search engines like Google track and store your search queries, building profiles for advertising purposes.
items.howTo: Change default search engine to DuckDuckGo, Startpage, or Searx. Chrome/Firefox: Settings > Search engine > Manage search engines. Set as default and remove tracking-based engines.

items.task: Install comprehensive ad and tracker blocker
items.why: Blocks advertisements, trackers, and malicious scripts that compromise privacy and can contain malware.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin (recommended) or similar privacy-focused ad blocker. Configure with additional filter lists like EasyPrivacy and Fanboy's Annoyance List for maximum protection.

items.why: Provides additional layers of protection against tracking, fingerprinting, and privacy violations that built-in browser settings might miss.
items.howTo: Install Privacy Badger (blocks trackers), Decentraleyes (protects against tracking via CDNs), and ClearURLs (removes tracking parameters from URLs). Avoid installing too many extensions to prevent fingerprinting.

items.why: Firefox offers extensive privacy configuration options through about:config that aren't available in the standard settings interface.
items.howTo: Type about:config in address bar. Set privacy.firstparty.isolate = true, network.cookie.cookieBehavior = 1, geo.enabled = false, and privacy.resistFingerprinting = true for maximum privacy.

items.why: Google's Privacy Sandbox still enables tracking through Topics API and other mechanisms, just in a different way than traditional cookies.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Privacy Sandbox > Turn off Ad topics, Site-suggested ads, and Ad measurement. Consider switching to privacy-first browsers like Incognito Browser instead.
